signature: Near-Harman tuning out of the box: clean elevated bass, neutral mids, smooth treble; very balanced with mild upper-mid energy.
correctionNotes: Already close to neutral, so corrections should be small and surgical.
A slight 3 kHz forwardness can be tamed for long sessions.
Sub-bass is solid; only add a touch if the listener wants extra rumble.

signature: Adaptive in-ear with a Harman-leaning tuning: clean elevated bass, neutral mids, and a slightly forward presence region; treble is smooth.
correctionNotes: Presence around 3 kHz can be a touch forward for long listening; a small dip helps.
Adaptive EQ already compensates for seal, so only modest corrections are appropriate.
Sub-bass is full thanks to in-ear seal; add very little extra low end.

signature: Planar with deep, authoritative bass and rich lower mids; treble is smooth but can feel slightly recessed in the upper presence region.
correctionNotes: Upper mids around 2–4 kHz are slightly polite; a small lift improves vocal intelligibility.
Lower mids can sound thick on warm recordings; a gentle dip near 200 Hz adds clarity.
Bass is already substantial, so additional sub-bass is rarely needed.

signature: Open-back clip-on with a clean, fast mid-bass punch, flat neutral mids, and a bright/energetic upper range with a prominent 3.5 kHz peak and 8 kHz treble presence.
correctionNotes: Low-bass rolls off below 100 Hz due to open clip-on seal; avoid heavy sub-bass boosts to prevent distortion and preserve the fast, punchy bass.
Upper midrange ear-gain peak around 3.5 kHz is energetic; a small cut smooths out shoutiness while maintaining clarity.
Treble peak around 8 kHz can be slightly sharp; a moderate cut reduces sibilance.
Lower mids (200-400 Hz) are clean but can benefit from a gentle body lift to add vocal warmth.
source: Official manufacturer frequency response and THD graphs from Aune.

signature: Closed-back studio reference: deep-extending but not warm bass with a mid-bass hump around 60-100 Hz, fairly neutral lower mids, a 1-1.2 kHz dip, a 1.9-2 kHz presence lift need, and upper-mid/lower-treble energy (around 2.5-6 kHz) that can sound sharp; high treble rolls off above 10 kHz.
correctionNotes: AutoEq/oratory1990 Harman OE 2018 correction uses a compound bass shape: low shelf @105 Hz -9.8 dB plus a very wide +18 dB peaking @81 Hz (Q0.36) and a -14.9 dB peaking @138 Hz (Q0.6) to convert the mid-bass hump into a Harman shelf. Net peak after this group is only ~4.5 dB.
Cut ~2.1 dB @1025 Hz (Q2.33) for the mild upper-bass/lower-mid dip region relative to target.
Boost ~+4.6 dB @1919 Hz (Q3.37) for the presence dip; cut -3.1 dB @2676 Hz (Q5.21) and -3.6 dB @5733 Hz (Q5.64) to tame sharp upper-mid/lower-treble.
Small +1.6 dB @3637 Hz (Q1.17) and +2.5 dB @9712 Hz (Q2.24); high shelf @10 kHz -3.2 dB for air/extension balance.
User preference on top of Harman: +3.0 dB low shelf @40 Hz for moderate sub-bass reinforcement (seal-dependent on closed-backs).
AutoEq preamp is -4.7 dB; with the sub-bass preference shelf use about -6 dB headroom.
source: AutoEq oratory1990 over-ear measurement (https://github.com/jaakkopasanen/AutoEq results/oratory1990/over-ear/Austrian Audio Hi-X60); dense GraphicEQ max +4.5 dB @~2 kHz. Corroborated by DIY-Audio-Heaven (deep bass extension with perfect seal, elevated upper mids/lower treble needing taming), Headphones.com DMS B&K 4128 (Harman-esque bass, treble glare above ~5 kHz), and ASR (bass peak ~100 Hz, peaking above 3 kHz).

signature: Open-back reference/studio tuning: extended but slightly lean bass vs Harman, mild low-mid thickness around 200-600 Hz, a noticeable 1.5-2 kHz presence dip, smooth forward upper mids, and an elevated 5-10 kHz treble that reads bright.
correctionNotes: Needs a ~+5.4 dB bass shelf at 105 Hz (Q0.7) plus ~+6 dB below 40 Hz to reach the Harman over-ear 2018 bass level; the driver extends cleanly to sub-bass (5 Hz spec, good measured extension).
Cut ~2.4 dB wide at 236 Hz (Q0.53) and ~1.5 dB at 592 Hz to clear low-mid boxiness.
The 1.5-2 kHz presence dip is the biggest midrange correction: ~+6.9 dB at 1659 Hz (Q1.76).
Small surgical fixes around the ear-gain region: -1.9 dB @ 2858 Hz (Q5.45), +2.9 dB @ 3426 Hz (Q5.91), -1.5 dB @ 4145 Hz (Q6).
Tame brightness with -4 dB at 5982 Hz (Q3.16) and a -1.5 dB high shelf at 10 kHz; Sonarworks measured a ~10 dB boost near 10 kHz vs neutral.
AutoEq preamp -6.5 dB covers the +6.9 dB peak; add more preamp when stacking a sub-bass preference shelf.
source: AutoEq oratory1990 over-ear measurement (https://github.com/jaakkopasanen/AutoEq results/oratory1990/over-ear/Austrian Audio Hi-X65); corroborated by Sonarworks GRAS review (neutral bass/low-mids, high-mid dip, ~10 dB treble lift near 10 kHz) and Sound On Sound (bright above ~5 kHz, even but unemphasized bass, slight low-mid thickness).

signature: V-shaped: elevated sub/mid-bass and a sharp treble peak around 8–9 kHz that reads as detailed but can be sibilant ('Beyer peak').
correctionNotes: Pronounced 8–9 kHz peak is fatiguing; a targeted cut here is the single most useful move.
Upper-mids around 250 Hz can sound slightly hollow; small bell lift improves vocal body.
Bass is already strong, so prefer cutting harsh treble over boosting bass.

signature: Aggressive V-shape: big sub-bass and a very prominent treble peak near 8 kHz, giving an airy but often harsh presentation.
correctionNotes: Strong 8 kHz peak is the defining flaw; cut it firmly to remove sibilance and listening fatigue.
A secondary 6 kHz region can also read as sharp on vocals.
Mids are slightly scooped; a gentle 1–2 kHz lift restores presence.

signature: Planar-clean and neutral-bright; fast tight bass, transparent mids, and an energetic treble with a mild peak around 5–6 kHz.
correctionNotes: Treble around 5–6 kHz can edge into harshness on bright recordings; a small cut smooths it.
Sub-bass extends well but is slightly light in quantity; a gentle low shelf adds body.
Mids are accurate, so avoid large mid-range moves.

signature: Semi-open single graphene DD IEM with a V-shaped tuning: elevated sub-bass and mid-bass, slightly recessed lower mids, forward upper-mid/presence peak around 3-5 kHz, an 8 kHz resonance bump, a 9-10 kHz dip, and relaxed air above 12 kHz. Detailed female vocals and airy treble per reviews, but bass lacks physicality and male voices can sound thin.
correctionNotes: Crinacle B&K 5128 measurement available via hangout.audio; AutoEQ correction computed toward IEF Preference 2025 (B&K 5128) target.
Mid-bass is elevated relative to IEF 2025: a 160 Hz bell cut around -2.5 dB tightens the low end without killing sub-bass extension.
Lower mids (300-500 Hz) are recessed: a +2 dB bell around 400 Hz restores body and male vocal weight.
Upper mids around 2.5-3 kHz need a +3 dB boost to reach IEF 2025 ear-gain; the stock tuning is forward at 4-5 kHz but recessed in the 2-3 kHz transition.
A 4.5-5 kHz presence peak needs a -3 to -4 dB cut to smooth the shouty edge.
The 8 kHz region shows elevated energy; treat conservatively (-2 to -3 dB) as part of this may be 5128 rig-dependent resonance.
A 9-10 kHz dip can accept a moderate +2.5 to +3 dB boost for treble sparkle, but avoid pushing above +3 dB in this region.
Ultra-treble above 12 kHz is unreliable on 5128; avoid narrow corrections there.
Semi-open design means sub-bass seal is moderate; do not chase extreme sub-bass boost.
source: Crinacle B&K Type 5128 (ITU-T P.57 Type 4.3) measurement via hangout.audio graph tool: https://graph.hangout.audio/iem/5128/?share=IEF_Preference_2025_(B%2526K_5128)_Target,HE_XiaoQiao . AutoEQ PEQ computed in-browser toward IEF Preference 2025 (B&K 5128) target, 20-15000 Hz, gain +/-12 dB, Q 0.5-2.0. Corroborated by Head-Fi reviews (Hifi Juegos, ybricko): https://www.head-fi.org/showcase/tangzu-harmonic-empire-xiaoqiao-iem.28377/ . Also measured on Aftersound squig.link (IEC 711 clone). Specs: single graphene DD, 104 dB @1 kHz, 9.8 ohm, semi-open, 4.4 mm balanced.

signature: Reference-neutral, slightly mid-forward, polite treble with a mild upper-mid lift; bass is fast but rolls off in the sub region.
correctionNotes: Sub-bass below ~40 Hz rolls off; a gentle low shelf restores weight without bloat.
Mild presence bump around 3 kHz can sound forward on bright tracks; a small dip tames it.
Treble is well controlled, so boosts above 8 kHz are usually unnecessary.
source: Aggregated measurement consensus (Crinacle, Oratory1990 style targets)

signature: Warm-neutral, smooth and relaxed; the classic 'veil' is a gentle upper-mid/lower-treble dip with a touch more mid-bass than the HD600.
correctionNotes: Lower treble (5–7 kHz) is recessed, so a small lift adds clarity and air.
Sub-bass roll-off below ~40 Hz benefits from a modest low shelf.
Already warm — avoid stacking extra mid-bass or it turns muddy.

signature: Consumer-warm with elevated bass and a smooth, slightly relaxed treble; mids are clean but bass can dominate at default.
correctionNotes: Mid-bass can mask lower mids; a small dip around 150–200 Hz cleans up muddiness.
Upper treble above 10 kHz is gently rolled off; a light high shelf adds air.
Default DSP already shapes the sound, so keep EQ moves modest.
